annotationRationale: Midpoint symmetry supplies the winning strategy. Absolute value expresses distances on the real line, and strict gap inequalities prove termination. The equivalent historical route is consolidated here; the planar distance formula is unnecessary.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is suitable for this combinatorial strategy game; no obvious subject repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Midpoint reflection proves that Bela wins for every allowed integer n, so A is correct. The current stem and choices are consistent. Random Math's supplemental transcription of choice D omits the oddness condition and differs from the current choice; the candidate correctly uses the current question.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: 2020_AMC_10B_Q16#midpoint-and-mirror-replies is independently verified and retained. 2020_AMC_10B_Q16#midpoint-reflection-and-finite-packing is merged into the same route: it describes the same strategy and has no stored worked explanation. LIVE and Random Math's mirror strategy agree. Random Math's guesses and integer-only trial games are omitted because they cannot prove optimal play on a real interval.
review.annotationCheck: Central symmetry is appropriately assessed. Absolute value and strict inequalities support legality and termination. Replacing the historical planar-distance node with cnm_007 accurately reflects the actual number-line argument.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is suitable for this combinatorial strategy game; no obvious subject repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Reflection preserves the interval and distances to the symmetric earlier set. A legal Jenn move is more than one unit from the midpoint, so its reflected reply is more than two units away. Symmetry is restored after each pair. The strict gap sum gives k-1<n and hence k≤n, proving finite termination and Bela's win.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The exact shared question and method are credited. Both inherited reference IDs from originalMethodProvenance.references are retained, alongside the current-question references. Reuse of the project explanation is correctly identified, and no official MAA authorship is claimed.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The explanation motivates the midpoint and separately checks interval membership, distances to earlier moves, distance to Jenn's new move, restoration of symmetry and termination. The proof covers real choices and endpoints.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_248 matches point symmetry restricted to the number line; cnm_007 supports absolute-difference distances; cnm_h018 supports the strict separation bound. The winning strategy is fully derived rather than hidden behind a broad game-theory label.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native symmetry, absolute-value and inequality topics fit the argument. The strategy and finite packing bound are explained consequences of those concepts.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The narrower G-CO.A.3 link provides symmetry overlap, but its listed polygon tasks are not performed. The supplied 6.NS.C.7 and partial 7.NS.A.1c/6.NS.C.7c links concern rational-number ordering or distances, whereas this game allows all real numbers. 6.NS.C.7d's contextual comparison is not exercised. cnm_h018 has no supplied US link; these are honest alignment limits.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All three direct nodes are used appropriately, with symmetry assessed and absolute value and inequalities supporting the complete strategy proof.
